scan.summary: This is an emergency action plan for Cascade Specialty Chemicals' Portland facility describing procedures for fires, chemical releases, medical emergencies, earthquakes, and other emergencies. It sets out alarm signals, evacuation routes and assembly points, employee accounting procedures, rescue and medical response, and training requirements for all 42 employees at the facility. The plan is kept accessible to employees and drills are held twice yearly.
scan.freshness_note: This plan was last revised in February 2021, nearly five years ago as of September 2026. Oregon OSHA requires emergency action plans to be reviewed and updated to reflect any changes in operations, layout, or procedures. A review is overdue and should be conducted immediately, particularly to verify that the 42-employee count, roster of wardens and first-aid responders, building layout, and procedures remain current.

gaps.title: Plan review currency
gaps.description: The plan states the facilities lead reviews it every January, but the document has not been revised since February 2021. Nearly five years have passed without an updated revision date. There is no evidence of January reviews or updates in that span.
gaps.fix: Conduct a full review of the plan against current building layout, staffing, procedures, and operations. If any changes are found, update the plan and set a new revision date. Maintain documentation of annual reviews as required.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA, based on federal OSHA 1910.38(a) which requires emergency action plans to be reviewed regularly and revised when needed to reflect changes
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

gaps.title: Missing emergency evacuation procedures for specific scenarios
gaps.description: The plan does not clearly specify procedures for different emergency types (fire vs. chemical release inside the building). While it describes shelter-in-place for outdoor chemical releases, it does not detail the procedure if a chemical release occurs inside the warehouse or laboratory.
gaps.fix: Add a section specifying distinct response procedures for: (1) fires, (2) chemical releases inside the building by area, (3) medical emergencies, (4) earthquakes. For internal chemical releases, specify isolation of the area, notification procedures, and whether evacuation or shelter-in-place applies.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA / federal OSHA 1910.38(a) requires specific procedures for anticipated emergencies
gaps.quote: For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place signal sounds.

gaps.title: Missing procedures for persons with disabilities or access needs
gaps.description: The plan does not address evacuation or assembly point procedures for employees with mobility limitations, hearing or vision impairments, or other disabilities that might affect their ability to evacuate safely or respond to alarms.
gaps.fix: Add a section on accommodations for employees with disabilities, including: designated assistance buddies, alternative alarm signals where needed, accessible assembly point areas, and procedures to ensure all employees can participate in drills.
gaps.citation: Americans with Disabilities Act Title I, and Oregon OSHA which adopts federal standards

gaps.title: Missing emergency contact procedures
gaps.description: The plan does not specify who is responsible for notifying emergency contacts, family members, or regulatory agencies (e.g., Oregon DEQ for chemical releases), or the procedure and timeline for such notifications.
gaps.fix: Add a section designating responsibility for emergency notifications, including: who contacts 911, who contacts the facility owner or corporate office, who reports to Oregon DEQ if required, and the order in which these notifications occur.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a); Oregon DEQ may require notification of releases under OAR 340-160

gaps.title: Missing alarm system testing and maintenance log
gaps.description: The plan states the alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month, but provides no reference to a testing log or maintenance record. No evidence is specified for this testing.
gaps.fix: Establish and maintain a written log of all alarm system tests, including date, time, person conducting the test, any issues found, and corrective actions taken. Reference this log in the plan.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a)(2) requires testing of alarm systems; NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code) requires documentation
gaps.quote: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead.

gaps.title: Missing incident coordinator contact information and procedures
gaps.description: The plan references an 'incident coordinator at the assembly point' but does not identify who holds this role, provide contact information, or specify what authority and decision-making power they have.
gaps.fix: Add a section identifying the incident coordinator(s) by name and title, providing backup coordinators, describing their role and authority, and specifying when they pass command to the fire department.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a) requires designation of persons responsible for emergency procedures
gaps.quote: Any person unaccounted for is reported at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire department on arrival.

gaps.title: Missing emergency medical response beyond first aid
gaps.description: The plan addresses first aid and minor injuries, but does not specify procedures for multiple casualties, severe injuries, triage, or coordination with emergency responders at the scene.
gaps.fix: Add procedures for mass casualty situations, including triage, identification of priority patients, communication with incoming EMS, and secure handling of injured persons.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a)(5) requires procedures for rescue and medical duties
gaps.quote: First aid is given at the assembly point by the trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster)

gaps.title: Missing procedures for securing hazardous materials after evacuation
gaps.description: The plan tells employees to 'secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds' before evacuation, but does not specify procedures for shutting down chemical processes, closing valves, or preventing spills during an emergency evacuation.
gaps.fix: Add a section specifying which chemical processes must be safely shut down before evacuation (if safe to do so), designating responsibility for this task, and the sequence in which it should occur.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a) and 1910.119 (Process Safety Management) require procedures to secure operations
gaps.quote: When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit.

gaps.title: Missing post-incident procedures
gaps.description: The plan does not specify procedures for re-entry after an emergency, investigation of the incident, communication with employees about what happened, or correction of identified hazards.
gaps.fix: Add a section covering: authorization for re-entry, incident investigation responsibility, communication with employees and families, and procedure for updating the plan based on lessons learned.
gaps.citation: Oregon OSHA 1910.38(a) and incident reporting requirements

scan.confidence_notes: I am confident in the document's basic content, structure, and the gaps identified. The document is clearly written and internally consistent. I have high confidence that the significant gaps listed (missing emergency contact procedures, incident coordinator identification, post-incident procedures, procedures for securing hazardous materials, and procedures for specific chemical release scenarios inside the building) are genuine omissions against Oregon OSHA / federal OSHA 1910.38 standards. I am high-confidence that the plan is significantly out of date; it has not been formally revised since February 2021 despite a stated commitment to annual review. I am not certain whether the two appendices (evacuation maps and roster) are truly missing from company records or merely not provided with this file. I cannot verify from this document alone whether the company holds the alarm testing log, drill records, or training records referenced above. I did not search for the specific Oregon OSHA rule citations; I am relying on federal OSHA 1910.38 as the governing standard, which Oregon OSHA adopts. Oregon may have additional or different requirements that I have not verified. The most time-sensitive action is to conduct the overdue plan review and update the revision date.
